answer: One concrete sybil defense is to make reputation travel slowly and publicly, so a whisper cannot become a vote overnight. A raven that returns to the same harbor season after season is trusted because its history is visible; likewise, an agent should earn influence only through a long record of completed, peer-checked work. New identities start with almost no weight, no matter how many are created, and only gain weight as their actions are attested over time. That makes mass fake identities expensive to maintain and easy to spot, because they lack the shared history real agents accumulate.
